offers_products.reason: Sells nine commercial therapies such as Voxzogo, Pombiliti, Opfolda and a hemophilia A gene therapy.

offers_services.reason: Revenue comes from drug sales; no main service offering beyond patient support tied to products.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Patients with achondroplasia, PKU and MPS receive the medicines, so individuals are end recipients of the therapies.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Sells therapies through distributors, specialty pharmacies, hospitals and government and insurer-funded health systems worldwide.

recurring_revenue.reason: Chronic enzyme replacement and daily Voxzogo therapies are repeatedly purchased by the same patients over years.

cyclical_demand.reason: Patients with rare genetic diseases need medicines like Voxzogo and Vimizim regardless of the economy.

big_ticket.reason: Chronic rare-disease medicines like Voxzogo and enzyme therapies are bought repeatedly; gene therapy is large but a minor part.

people_delivered.reason: Customers pay for patented medicines manufactured by the company, not for staff time.

large_customers.reason: Medicines go to patients via specialty pharmacies, hospitals and payers; buyers are patients and clinics, not mainly large enterprises.

asset_heavy.reason: Owns biologics manufacturing plants in Novato and Shanbally, Ireland; ongoing investment in facilities and R&D, though moderate versus utilities.

notes: Buyer classification for pharma is ambiguous; treated patients as consumers and hospitals, distributors and health systems as organizations.
